sources.title: Artificial intelligence models for predicting acute kidney injury in the intensive care unit: a systematic review of modeling methods, data utilization, and clinical applicability

evidence.text: This systematic review comprehensively evaluated the AI models for the prediction of AKI in the ICU.
Public ICU datasets were widely used.
Across the 47 included studies, models including LR, RF, XGBoost, and SVM were the most commonly used.
Model performance was primarily evaluated using AUROC, while other metrics and calibration were less reported.
Overall, although progress in modeling approaches is evident, limitations in generalizability, transparency, and clinical translation remain.
The PROBAST assessment suggested a high risk of bias in most studies, especially in the analysis domain.

location.section: Risk of bias and clinical applicability

evidence.text: Only 14 studies conducted external validation, and 33 applied interpretation tools, mainly SHAP.
Our findings highlight the advantages of AI models in handling complex ICU data, capturing temporal dynamics, and supporting early prediction of AKI.
